description:
The Russian President has told African leaders that his country is a better partner than the West.
It happened at the third Russia-Africa Summit being held in Moscow.  
Vladimir Putin says Russian companies operate in Africa on an equal footing, accusing Western countries of still focusing on exploiting the continent's resources.
Some African nations in recent years, have turned to Russia for security assistance.
Trade and economic ties are also growing. 
And Russia has highlighted the importance of what it calls a 'multipolar world' - while it seeks support from the Global South to counter Western pressure for the Ukraine war.
So, what are Russia and African countries getting out of this gathering? 

Presenter: Dareen Abughaida

Guests:

Beverly Ochieng - Associate Director at Control Risks, which focuses on Francophone Africa and the Sahel region. 

Andrey Kortunov - Russian foreign affairs analyst and the former Director General of the Russian International Affairs Council.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
When his six-month-old daughter fell ill, Geng Munien Bol carried her for hours to reach a hospital. The clinic near their home in South Sudan had closed after cuts to US foreign aid. After several trips to the hospital, Bol's daughter died.

In A Thousand Cuts, Fault Lines travels to South Sudan to investigate the consequences of the dismantling of United States humanitarian aid by the administration of US President Donald Trump. Hind Hassan meets families struggling to get treatment and doctors who say the cuts are costing lives. A former senior official from the US Agency for International Development (USAID) reveals how warnings about the deadly consequences went unheeded, while an internal memo sheds light on the failure to deliver promised waivers for lifesaving aid.
